column1: # Requirements for the Mica::Brotli encoder (milestone Z6, the pure-Crystal
# Brotli encoder): what RFC 7932 requires of a compliant compressor, the
# public API and the properties the encoder keeps. google/brotli 1.2.1 is the
# reference: fuzz/brotli_encode_campaign.cr decodes every stream Mica writes
# in libbrotlidec and in Mica. Format: id<TAB>section<TAB>summary.

column3: Empty, one byte, all-zero, random, text, JSON and HTML inputs decode to the original at every quality from 0 to 11
Every window from 10 to 24 bits is written in the stream header and no match reaches past (1 << WBITS) - 16 bytes
google/brotli v1.2.1's test files decode to the original at every quality
Input larger than a metablock is split into several, each at most 2^24 bytes, with matches reaching back across them
A metablock that does not compress is stored uncompressed (never as the last metablock), so the output grows by a few bytes at most
Static dictionary references (whole words and words with their last bytes omitted) are used where no backward match exists
The same input and options give the same bytes
A quality outside 0 to 11 or a window outside 10 to 24 raises ArgumentError; Writer#read raises IO::Error
Writer output decodes to the input for any sequence of write sizes and flushes
Writer memory is bounded: it drops history older than the window and keeps matching
flush ends on a byte boundary with an empty metadata metablock, so the bytes so far decode everything written before it; an idle flush adds no bytes
A Writer closed with nothing written produces a valid empty stream
A Writer fed one piece decodes like Brotli.encode output
